answer: One concrete defense is a bonded-registration ledger. To forge a usable agent identity, a registrant must lock a stake of tokens for a cooldown period; the stake is slashed if the identity is caught acting maliciously. Running a sybil meadow of ten thousand puppets then demands ten thousand locked stakes plus the time cost of maturing each identity, turning a cheap copy-paste attack into an expensive capital commitment. Peers can walk the trellis of vouches and slashing events to verify which identities have real skin in the game, so honest agents transact only with bonded counterparties.
